\[
D(p) = \min_{q \notin X} \lVert p - q \rVert,
\qquad
M(X) = \{ p \in X : \text{the disk of radius } D(p) \text{ at } p \text{ is maximal in } X \}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(X\): The foreground
- \(D(p)\): The distance of p to the background
- \(M(X)\): The medial axis

X is the foreground and D the Euclidean distance to the background. Blum defined the medial axis as the centers of the maximal disks, those that fit in X and lie in no larger disk that fits. Together with D, the axis describes X completely. On a pixel grid the exact axis breaks into pieces. The scikit-image code thins the foreground instead, removing pixels in order of increasing distance as long as connectivity is kept, so the axis stays connected and one pixel wide. Ties are broken in a random order, which the filter fixes with the seed 0.
